_comment: The timing tail, by transiting body. Keyed body, then direction:
[0] is applying, still coming to exact, [1] is separating, already past.
Plain English, no astrology. A reader does not know what 'past exact' or
'still applying' means, and the sentence that ends a card is the one they
are most likely to finish reading. So: 'this peaked this morning and is
easing off', not 'past exact now, and thinning out through the afternoon'.
None of these names a body, because the card prints that from the chart
underneath. None of these introduces a new subject: 'this' is the reading
the body has just given. And each one has to survive being read directly
after an instruction, since that is what every body now ends on.
A day's nine cards are mostly driven by whichever body is moving fastest,
so several of them share a transit body and a direction. With one clause
per state, four cards a morning ended on the same sentence, which is the
single most visible way an assembled page gives itself away. reading.js
walks this list rather than seeding it, so two cards in one render cannot
